title: Introspection: Quantization tradeoff matrix and kernel-level benchmarking
content:
Purpose
---
Quick, pragmatic exploration of the multi-dimensional trade space between numeric approximation (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ variants) and kernel choice as it affects both tail latency and application-level quality. This doc captures a lightweight matrix-style sweep we ran to expose non-obvious interactions (kernel selection x layer type x prefix length) and to produce a set of actionable heuristics for the routing layer and the kernel selector.

High-level summary (TL;DR)
---
- Different approximation formats do not form a simple Pareto curve; kernel implementation details cause crossovers depending on sequence length and KV-cache hit rate.
- AWQ variants in our builds show the best cost/latency for short chat-style prefixes (<128 tokens) on A100-like hardware when using the fused-matmul kernels, but quality degradation on instruction-following tasks is less predictable.
- GPTQ with per-channel calibration + fallback mixing reduces catastrophic quality drops on dense-reasoning prompts at the cost of ~6–12% latency penalty vs the fastest INT8 kernel.
- FP8 paths maintain quality with smaller latency improvements vs FP16; depending on kernel (tensor core utilization) FP8 sometimes hurts throughput because of additional format conversion overheads in the runtime.

Testbed and constraints
---
- HW: 4x A100 40GB (single-process worker), and a 2x H100 80GB cluster profile for cross-checks.
- OS/container: ubuntu-22.04, cuda 12.2, cuBLAS/cuDNN matched to kernels commit.
- Model family: LLaMA-2-13B and a narrow-reasoning 30B finetune used as representative fast/slow nets.
- Request mix: 60% short-chat (avg len 40 tokens, prefix-heavy), 25% moderate (avg 256 tokens), 15% long-generation (avg 1024 tokens). KV cache warmup simulated with prefix reuse rates {0%, 25%, 75%}.
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p99 tail latency (single-request), tokens/sec (throughput with 512 concurrent clients), average per-token GPU time, wall-clock inference cost proxy (GPU-seconds/token), and quality: LM perplexity on holdout, instruction-response accuracy on a curated 400-sample eval set (mix: code, math, commonsense), and a small 50-shot reasoning regression test (hard cases).

Methodology notes (how we ran it)
---
- Swept formats: baseline FP16 (reference), INT8-GPTQ (2 variants: per-layer-scale vs per-channel), AWQ-quant (fused kernels), and mixed FP8 (E4M3-like config).
- Kernel implementations: vendor-tuned fused-matmul, our custom tiled-kernel v2 (fewer registers, lower occupancy), and an experiment with CUDA cooperative groups microkernel (for better warp-level cache reuse).
- For each cell in the matrix (format × kernel × model × prefix-length × kv-hit-rate) we replayed a fixed set of 1k prompts and recorded deterministic seeds to allow error reproduction.
- Quality measured as delta vs FP16 baseline: delta-perplexity, delta-instr-accuracy (fraction correct), and a free-form human review sample (20 cases flagged when instr-accuracy drop > 6%).
- We used the runtime profiler hooks for per-kernel timers and the serving trace to map request phases (embedding, attention, feedforward) to kernel invocations.

Key results (selected, aggregated into a tradeoff matrix)
---
1) Short-prefix, high-reuse (chatbot-style, prefix 32–64, KV hit 75%):
   - AWQ + fused-matmul: +55% tokens/sec vs FP16, p99 latency down 22%, instruction-accuracy drop median 1.7% (acceptable for many PLG use cases).
   - INT8-GPTQ (per-channel) + tiled-kernel v2: +40% tokens/sec, p99 down 12%, but better stability on edge-case arithmetic prompts.
   - FP8 mixed paths: +28% tokens/sec, no meaningful accuracy regression. However, conversion overheads increased p50 slightly.

2) Moderate prefix, mixed reuse (prefix 256, KV hit 25%):
   - Kernel crossover observed: fused-matmul had higher single-op throughput but suffered from more kernel launch overheads at moderate sequence lengths, giving tiled-kernel v2 an edge for p90 throughput.
   - AWQ latency advantages shrink; quality variance increases for instruction-following tasks (drop up to 5% on one subtask).

3) Long generations (prefix 512–1024, KV hit 0%):
   - GPTQ variants show the best quality retention; INT8 fused implementations deliver the highest raw throughput but with several prompts showing token-level hallucination escalation (we flagged 12/1k prompts).
   - FP8 fails to meaningfully beat FP16 in throughput on H100 due to format conversion overhead in our runtime path; we suspect a missing cuTENSOR path that could flip the result.

4) Tail-latency and jitter observations:
   - Certain kernels create long outliers tied to temporary register spilling in deep layers (interaction with fused attention kernels). These outliers appear more frequently in INT8 fused kernels on model variants with larger hidden dimensions.
   - Mixed-precision fallback (detect quality metric spike -> switch to per-layer mixed FP16/GPTQ) reduces p99 by up to 18% in our synthetic load tests.

Detailed micro-findings (raw notes)
---
- Layer 18–24 (middle MLP blocks) are where GPTQ per-channel vs per-layer diverges most: per-channel keeps activation distributions better, reducing catastrophic spikes in perplexity.
- Kernel 'A' (fused-matmul) shows 8–11% faster steady-state throughput but is sensitive to sequence-length variance because it does less work batching. Kernel 'B' (tiled-v2) is more consistent across seq-lengths.
- AWQ math: quant scales were good for attention weights, but output quantization on feedforward outputs caused softmax scaling shifts for some instruction prompts. Raising reconstruction steps in AWQ training prevented the worst drops (experiment: 3 vs 7 reconstruction iterations).
- Interaction: using our runtime's prefetcher with AWQ fused kernels sometimes increased p99 due to staggered map/unmap GPU memory events — prefetcher tune needed.

Actionable heuristics (for routing + kernel selector)
---
1) Default path for short-chat: AWQ + fused-matmul with KV-aware batching and prefer per-request prefix < 128. Provide an opt-out  parameter for customers requiring max fidelity.
2) For mixed workloads expose a 'stability' profile that selects GPTQ-per-channel + tiled-kernel v2 when the prompt matches arithmetic/reasoning intent (we can detect via a small intent classifier).
3) Long-generation / high-consistency workloads: prefer mixed FP16/GPTQ fallback mode; add automatic canary for first 3 generations to detect hallucination spikes and switch to safe path.
4) Add a runtime flag to disable our prefetcher for AWQ fused-matmul until we fix the unmap jitter (SERV-6821).

Unresolved questions / follow-ups
---
- Why does FP8 perform poorly on H100 in our path but not in vendor microbenchmarks? Hypothesis: missing optimized cuTENSOR+tensorcore conversion path; need to reproduce with a clean vendor stack (no custom kernel loader).
- Are the hallucination spikes a data/quant interaction (specific tokens causing overflow) or a kernel numerical instability? Plan: instrument activation histograms and repro cases at full-precision to compare.
- Can we incorporate an inexpensive per-request quick-check (micro-eval of 3 short probe prompts) to decide routing to stable vs fast path? Prototype needed.

Appendix A: Representative commands and flags
---
- Runner: ./serve --model ll-13b --format awq --kernel fused-matmul --kv-reuse 0.75 --profile hooks:on --batchshape auto --prefetcher on
- Profiling: python tools/trace_parser.py --trace out.trace --summaries --per-kernel
- Reproduction: tests/repro/quant_spike_repro.sh --seed 427 --format int8-gptq --kernel fused-matmul

Appendix B: Quick reproduction cases (ids)
---
- CASE-973: long-math-prompt-3 — shows hallucination with INT8-fused on ll-13b (seeded reproduction: see linked artifact PR)
- CASE-981: short-instruction-drop-8 — AWQ softmax scale issue; raising reconstruction loops fixes locally

Notes to reviewers
---
- This is deliberately pragmatic — not a formal paper. The goal is to surface operational knobs for immediate runtime policies and to justify a small engineering follow-up: two kernel patches (tiled kernel tuning + fused kernel launch batching) and a fallback + probe flow.
- Priorities: 1) stop-gap runtime flags (prefetcher disable, fallback route) 2) reproduce FP8 on bare vendor stack 3) instrument per-layer histograms for live runs.

Owner/next steps
---

End of doc.
